### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**2** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them. ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/mcp/package.json`, `packages/mcp/vitest.config.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/mcp/package.json`, `packages/mcp/vitest.config.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **12** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c513d62acdd342745bbfe29786ba4b644cd934fc` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `77ddeec7dd6e8c114e1f1bfa3b880a4387b96a11` — the merge of head `f12cb94021cd6382dc1147883b82183b74373587` into base `c513d62acdd342745bbfe29786ba4b644cd934fc`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 77ddeec7dd6e8c114e1f1bfa3b880a4387b96a11 && git checkout 77ddeec7dd6e8c114e1f1bfa3b880a4387b96a11
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin c513d62acdd342745bbfe29786ba4b644cd934fc f12cb94021cd6382dc1147883b82183b74373587 && git checkout -B drift-repro c513d62acdd342745bbfe29786ba4b644cd934fc && git merge --no-ff f12cb94021cd6382dc1147883b82183b74373587

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c513d62acdd342745bbfe29786ba4b644cd934fc
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## L1 review · 2026-11-17T12:55Z

L1: ACCEPT
Head-sha: f12cb94021cd6382dc1147883b82183b74373587

Read at this exact head: the 7 files (+221/−7), the body, card #34787, claim 6946458372, amendment 6948225307 and os-dev-report 6948178219. `check-governed-merges`: not governed, 228 lines. Check-runs on this sha: 69 total, 60 success, 9 skipped, 0 failed or pending.

### Must-fix

None.

### Should-fix

None.

### Checklist

- **Shape:** draft, `Closes #34787`. Both declaration lines (`Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`) are in the body and the changeset, and they match the claim. No export of `@objectstack/mcp` grows: `StdioDataBridgeDeps.i18n` is an optional member of an internal deps bag. So `no` holds, and no seat L2 is owed.
- **Surface:** `stdio-data-bridge.ts`, `plugin.ts`, `package.json` (the claim's rest-import option), a card-named test and the changeset are inside the claim. `vitest.config.ts`, the `@objectstack/service-analytics` devDependency and the `pnpm-lock.yaml` importer links are covered by amendment 6948225307 as route-forced adds. No unrelated files.
- **Changeset:** one `@objectstack/mcp` patch, the only published package whose src moved. It says the new runtime dependency on `@objectstack/rest`.
- **Change:** `loadDatasets` runs `translateMetaList(…, 'dataset', items)` with inputs that mirror `packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts` on the HTTP door. The i18n service is resolved per call, and a throwing resolver reads as none. The merged protocol is the packaged base. The locale is `metaRequestLocale(undefined, i18n)`, which falls back to the i18n default, the same answer HTTP gives with no `Accept-Language`. A non-array result falls back to the untranslated list. `@objectstack/rest` does not depend on `@objectstack/mcp`, so there is no cycle (`check:workspace-manifest-cycles` exit 0 in the report). `plugin-auth` already imports `translateMetaList` the same way. The term matcher, `candidates` and the HTTP door are untouched, as the claim requires.
- **Tests:** real commands are given. The whole mcp package passes (1230 tests) and typecheck passes. The new test has 4 cases: zh-CN default, en default, a throwing resolver, and no i18n service. The zh-CN case runs the real `matchDatasetTerms` and pins 总金额 and 阶段 as `label`. The ablation of the return line turns the zh-CN case red, and the restore is blob-verified. The test reaches the bridge through a relative import, so no `dist/` is on its path.
- **Acceptance:** met. Live readings on app-crm copies show stdio equal to HTTP with no header, under both a zh-CN and an en default. The "Avg Deal Size misses under zh-CN" reading is the #34720 ruling (6946563869), accepted in the amendment. It is not a gap of this card.
- **Docs made false:** none found. `git grep` over `content/docs`, `skills`, `docs` and the mcp README at this head turns up no text that says stdio serves datasets untranslated. The `plugin.ts` comment that calls the workspace default the only stdio locale stays true. ADR-0149 D2 ("localized at the metadata boundary") is what this PR now satisfies on stdio.
- **UI strings:** none added.

### Notes

- N1: The body's Human Minimum leaves the *Before Submitting* box unticked. This is a nit.
- N2: The report's open question (keep the dispatch's `<!-- signed: … -->` HTML-comment line, which os-dev.md forbids) is the seat's convention call. It does not affect this verdict.
- N3: As the body says, a resolved i18n service whose `getLocales`/`getTranslations` throws reaches the executor as a degraded read on both transports. That case has no pin. It is parity, not a regression.
- N4: `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` was NOT MEASURED locally (exit 3, missing dists). CI's `Lint & Repo Gates` ran it on a full build and is green on this sha.

Under the "only nit-level findings open at landing" standard, nothing here blocks landing.
